Supplementary Table 4; Supplementary Note 7, simulation paragraphs
post_operative (P1 sess04-09 x6 + P2 sess03/05/06/08/09 x5); the simulation uses 9 of the 11 sessions. n = 2 patients, case-level.
3 s: a trial is included when at least 3 s of decoder output remain after the decoder's 4 s start-up
window-matched: the walker's own phase replayed on exactly the decoded window of each of the 130 decoded trials, driven from trial 2 s by its own goniometer

Each contrast is tested on the per-trial paired difference d = A - B (pairs matched on session x trial_idx; in a vs-zero test d is the value itself), NaN dropped, with a linear mixed model d ~ 1 + (1 | session) (session ids are unique across the two patients), fitted by REML in statsmodels MixedLM (optimizers lbfgs, powell and cg; of the fits that converge with a finite intercept SE and log-likelihood, the one with the largest log-likelihood is kept): the fixed intercept is the mean difference and the session random intercept accounts for trials within a session being correlated. Per-patient rows fit the same model to that patient's trials (4 and 5 sessions). Its Wald p is p_used for every contrast; Shapiro-Wilk on the residuals and the two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p are reported in the Source Data only. Stars *** / ** / * / ns at 0.001 / 0.01 / 0.05 on p_used. Boxes, lines and in-figure numbers show medians, descriptively.

Walker (window-matched): the reference walker's own gait phase replayed on exactly the decoded window of each decoded trial; a ceiling, not a null. Decoded: the patient's EEG-decoded per-joint phase driving the normative gait template. Coordination null: the inter-joint phase relationship destroyed, timing kept. In-phase null: the decoded phases replaced by one common phase, so that all six joints move in phase. Every condition drives the biped from 2 s into the trial: the Walker by the reference walker's goniometer signal; the Decoded condition and both nulls by the decoder's readout before temporal refinement until the onset of the final decoder output (4 s) and by the final output thereafter, the nulls being built on that whole drive. All four conditions share one set of 130 trials. Source Data field: column "condition" = 'wphase_matched' with column "stage" = 'calib' (Walker; walker_matched_rhythm.csv, walker_matched_traces_x.csv.gz), and 'dphase', 'dphase_iscr', 'dphase_uscr' with column "stage" = 'confirm' (Decoded, Coordination null, In-phase null; rhythm_metrics.csv, traces_x.csv.gz); column "phase_src" = 'k1' and column "lam" = 0.0 for every condition.

Forward displacement over the 3.0 s after the onset of the final decoder output (m) (m): the simulated hip displacement of the physics rollout 3.0 s after the onset of the final decoder output (trial time 4 s; the biped is driven from trial time 2 s), measured from the hip position at that onset: the last recorded sample at or before 3.0 s after the onset on the 40 ms recording grid. A displacement in metres, not a gait speed and not a clinical walking distance. | Cadence (steps s⁻¹) (steps s⁻¹): the number of advancing left-right support transitions divided by the rollout duration. A transition advances when the incoming support foot lands at least 0.01 m in front of the outgoing one, so only forward steps are counted. | Step length (m) (m): the net forward hip displacement of the rollout divided by its number of advancing steps, that is, the mean forward progression per advancing step. A rollout with no advancing step has no step length and is dropped. Negative values indicate net backward progression. | Advancing-step count imbalance (dimensionless): the absolute difference between the numbers of left and right advancing steps divided by their sum: 0 for perfectly alternating left-right stepping, 1 when every advancing step falls on the same side. | Rollouts moving backward (%) (%): the percentage of the condition's rollouts whose 3.0 s forward displacement is negative. | Rollouts with a fall (n) (count): the number of rollouts in which trunk pitch exceeded 60 deg from vertical or hip height fell below half the standing hip height, at any time from trial time 2 s.

Within a single patient the test_rule model keeps its session random intercept (patient 1: 4 sessions, patient 2: 5), so the per-patient rows fit d ~ 1 + (1 | session) to that patient's rollouts, test_used 'LME (within patient)'. Every contrast row names the model it used in the `model` column.
Every contrast is paired on (session, trial_idx): the window-matched walker replays the same trials over exactly the decoded samples, and each null re-runs those trials with the phases swapped.

75 pooled values are re-derived here and asserted equal to the live Fig. 7 panel Source Data on every run: medians_per_condition of fig7_sim_cadence / fig7_sim_step_symmetry / sup_fig7_sim_step_length, endpoint_stats of fig7_sim_trajectories, and every pooled contrast row of the four *_stats.csv files (n, mean difference, p_used, test used, star). The script writes nothing if any value disagrees.
Median [25th, 75th percentile] over rollouts for every quantity; rollouts moving backward is a percentage and rollouts with a fall a count. Fallen rollouts are NOT dropped.
Reported uncorrected. The endpoints are not independent: the two nulls re-run the same trials, and cadence, step length and asymmetry all read the same advancing-step array.

MuJoCo behavioural outcomes only: no GRF, no contact force, no balance / stability / efficacy claim. Rollouts are nested in sessions and in 2 patients, so every p value is a trial-level test, not a population-level one.
